# origin compute commands

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py from `origin --help` of the release scripts/origin-cli.version pins (v1.19.0).
     Do not edit by hand: fix the help text in origincloudhq/cli, or scripts/cli_reference_overrides.yml, and rerun. -->

This page lists every `origin compute` command. For the options every `origin` command accepts, see [Global options](../../platform/reference/cli.md#global-options); for how `--project` and `--zone` default, see [Use the CLI](../../platform/access/cli.md#set-a-default-project-zone-and-region).

## origin compute

Compute service: instances, images, key pairs, volume attachments, and the instance types and image families on offer. Resource names are given as their parts (`--project`, `--zone`, `--instance`), or the resource's flag takes a whole name; `--project` and `--zone` default to the profile's `default-project` and `default-zone`.

Every `origin compute` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host: `https://compute.origincloudapis.eu`, or `https://compute.{region}.origincloudapis.eu` when the profile names a `region`. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). A list without `--zone` looks up the zones at the location service, not here; `ORIGINCLOUD_LOCATION_ENDPOINT` sends that lookup elsewhere. Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_COMPUTE_ENDPOINT`. |

### get-instance-type

Returns an instance type.

```sh
origin compute get-instance-type [OPTIONS] --instance-type <INSTANCE_TYPE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--instance-type <INSTANCE_TYPE>` | yes | The type to return, `instanceTypes/{instance_type}`. Its id, or its whole name, `instanceTypes/{instance_type}`. |

### list-instance-types

Lists every instance type, including those no longer offered, which instances launched as them still report: check `available` before launching as one.

```sh
origin compute list-instance-types [OPTIONS]
```

This command takes no options of its own.

### get-image-family

Returns an image family.

```sh
origin compute get-image-family [OPTIONS] --image-family <IMAGE_FAMILY>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--image-family <IMAGE_FAMILY>` | yes | The family to return, `imageFamilies/{image_family}`. Its id, or its whole name, `imageFamilies/{image_family}`. |

### list-image-families

Lists every image family, including those no longer offered: check `available` before launching from one.

```sh
origin compute list-image-families [OPTIONS]
```

This command takes no options of its own.

### get-image

Returns one of the project's own images.

```sh
origin compute get-image [OPTIONS] --image <IMAGE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--image <IMAGE>` | yes | The image to return. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. |

### list-images

Lists the project's own images in a zone, oldest first. The public images are listed by `ListPublicImages`.

```sh
origin compute list-images [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone to list, such as `eu-central1-az1`. Without it, every zone that offers the service is listed, in catalog order; the profile's `default-zone` isn't used for lists. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most images to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |

### create-image

Creates an image from the project's protected snapshots in the zone. The snapshots can't be unprotected while the image exists.

```sh
origin compute create-image [OPTIONS] --description <DESCRIPTION> --root-device <ROOT_DEVICE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--description <DESCRIPTION>` | yes | What the image holds, as you describe it. |
| `--default-user <DEFAULT_USER>` | no | The account an instance launched from the image logs in as, unless the launch names another: a POSIX user name of at most 32 lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or an underscore, and not `root`. `cloud` when left empty. |
| `--root-device <ROOT_DEVICE>` | yes | The device name of the disk the image boots from: one of the `--block-device`' `device`. |
| `--block-device <KEY=VALUE,...>` | no | The image's disks, each created for an instance launched from it. One element as comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs; repeat the flag for more. A key is a field's name, with `_` or `-`. The keys: `device`, required: The device name the disk appears under on every instance launched from the image: `vda` to `vdz` but `vdc`, unique within the image. `size_gib`, required: The disk's size in GiB, at least the snapshot's. `source_snapshot`: The protected snapshot the disk is created from, in the image's project and zone; an empty disk when left empty. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/snapshots/{snapshot}`. A value with a comma in it goes through `--block-devices-json` too. |
| `--block-devices-json <JSON>` | no | The whole list as the API's JSON, an array of objects whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. A resource name in a field of the message itself is completed with `--project` and `--zone`, as in its KEY=VALUE form; one nested deeper must be whole. Instead of `--block-device`. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | no | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's image instead of creating a second one. One is generated when not given. |

### update-image

Changes an image's description or tags.

```sh
origin compute update-image [OPTIONS] --image <IMAGE> <--description <DESCRIPTION>|--tag <KEY=VALUE>|--no-tags>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--image <IMAGE>` | yes | The image to change. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. |
| `--description <DESCRIPTION>` | one of `--description`, `--tag`, `--no-tags` | What the image holds, as you describe it. Left as it is when not given. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | one of `--description`, `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-tags` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-tags` | one of `--description`, `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Remove all of its tags. |

### delete-image

Deletes an image. Instances launched from it are unaffected.

```sh
origin compute delete-image [OPTIONS] --image <IMAGE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--image <IMAGE>` | yes | The image to delete. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-instance

Returns an instance. A terminated instance can be read by name for a day after it was terminated.

```sh
origin compute get-instance [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The instance to return. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. |

### list-instances

Lists the instances in a zone, oldest first. A terminated instance is listed for two hours after it was terminated. For every zone's instances, list the zones whose `services` name `compute` with the location service (`location.origincloudapis.eu`), then each zone's instances.

```sh
origin compute list-instances [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone to list, such as `eu-central1-az1`. Without it, every zone that offers the service is listed, in catalog order; the profile's `default-zone` isn't used for lists. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most instances to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |

### create-instance

Launches an instance. The operation is done once the instance is `RUNNING`, or failed once it is `FAILED`, with the reason in `stateReason`; a failed instance still exists, and can be started again or deleted.

```sh
origin compute create-instance [OPTIONS] --instance-type <INSTANCE_TYPE> --key-pair <KEY_PAIR> --network-interface <NETWORK_INTERFACE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--service-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--instance-type <INSTANCE_TYPE>` | yes | The instance type, `instanceTypes/{instance_type}`, such as `instanceTypes/gp1.core.2`: one whose `available` is true. Changing it needs the instance `STOPPED`. Its id, or its whole name, `instanceTypes/{instance_type}`. |
| `--image <IMAGE>` | no | The image the boot volume is created from, in the instance's zone: one of the project's own, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`, or a public one, `zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. Set exactly one of `--image` and `--image-family`; launched from a family, this is the public image the family resolved to. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}` or `zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. |
| `--image-family <IMAGE_FAMILY>` | no | The image family to launch the current public image of, `imageFamilies/{image_family}`. Set exactly one of `--image` and `--image-family`. Empty when the instance was launched from an image. Its id, or its whole name, `imageFamilies/{image_family}`. |
| `--key-pair <KEY_PAIR>` | yes | The key pair whose public key is installed for `--login-user`, in the instance's project. Its id, completed with `--project`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/keyPairs/{key_pair}`. |
| `--login-user <LOGIN_USER>` | no | The account to log in as: a user created at first boot that holds the key pair. A POSIX user name of at most 32 lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or an underscore, and not `root`. The image's `defaultUser` when left empty. |
| `--boot-volume <KEY=VALUE,...>` | no | The boot volume: its size and storage class at launch, and the volume. The image's size on the default storage class when left out. As comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs. A key is a field's name, with `_` or `-`. The keys: `size_gib`: The size in GiB the volume was created with, at least the image's size; the image's size when left at 0. Grow the volume itself to resize it; this keeps the size at launch. `storage_class`: The storage class, `storageClasses/{storage_class}` of the persistent volume service; the default class when left empty. Its id, or its whole name, `storageClasses/{storage_class}`. A value with a comma in it goes through `--boot-volume-json` too. |
| `--boot-volume-json <JSON>` | no | As the API's JSON, an object whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. A resource name in a field of the message itself is completed with `--project` and `--zone`, as in its KEY=VALUE form; one nested deeper must be whole. Instead of `--boot-volume`. |
| `--network-interface <NETWORK_INTERFACE>` | yes | The network interfaces, in device order, the boot interface first; exactly one today. Each is an existing interface in the instance's project and zone that nothing else holds, created with the network service: its subnet and security groups are the instance's. Terminating the instance releases it, and it stays. An instance launched before interfaces were named at launch shows the interface created for it, which is deleted with the instance. Each by its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/networkInterfaces/{network_interface}`. Repeat for more. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | no | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | no | The service account the instance runs as, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`: a `WORKLOAD` service account of the instance's organization that isn't deleted. Launching with one, or updating the instance to one, needs `iam.service_account.act_as` on the organization as well; an update that leaves it empty removes it, and a terminated instance's can't change. Empty for an instance that runs as none. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of launching a second instance. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### update-instance

Changes an instance's type, tags or service account. A new `--instance-type` needs the instance `STOPPED`, and is refused with `FAILED_PRECONDITION` otherwise; it takes effect at the next start. A larger type is checked against the same vCPU quota a launch is. The operation is done once the instance shows the change.

```sh
origin compute update-instance [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE> <--instance-type <INSTANCE_TYPE>|--tag <KEY=VALUE>|--no-tags|--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--service-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The instance to change. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. |
| `--instance-type <INSTANCE_TYPE>` | one of `--instance-type`, `--tag`, `--no-tags`, `--service-account` | The instance type, `instanceTypes/{instance_type}`, such as `instanceTypes/gp1.core.2`: one whose `available` is true. Changing it needs the instance `STOPPED`. Its id, or its whole name, `instanceTypes/{instance_type}`. Left as it is when not given. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | one of `--instance-type`, `--tag`, `--no-tags`, `--service-account` | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-tags` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-tags` | one of `--instance-type`, `--tag`, `--no-tags`, `--service-account` | Remove all of its tags. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | one of `--instance-type`, `--tag`, `--no-tags`, `--service-account` | The service account the instance runs as, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`: a `WORKLOAD` service account of the instance's organization that isn't deleted. Launching with one, or updating the instance to one, needs `iam.service_account.act_as` on the organization as well; an update that leaves it empty removes it, and a terminated instance's can't change. Empty for an instance that runs as none. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. Left as it is when not given. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of changing the instance again. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### delete-instance

Terminates an instance: its guest is stopped for good, its network interfaces are released, `AVAILABLE` again with their addresses (one created for it at launch is deleted), and its boot volume is deleted with it unless a snapshot of it exists. Other attached volumes are detached and kept. Terminating a terminated instance changes nothing. The operation is done once the instance is `TERMINATED`.

```sh
origin compute delete-instance [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The instance to terminate. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### start-instance

Starts a `STOPPED` or `FAILED` instance. It keeps its name, its addresses and its volumes, and may come back on another machine. Starting a running instance changes nothing; it is refused while the instance is `INITIALIZING`, `STOPPING` or `SHUTTING_DOWN`. The operation is done once the instance is `RUNNING`, or failed once it is `FAILED`.

```sh
origin compute start-instance [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The instance to start. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### stop-instance

Stops a running instance: its guest is shut down, and it keeps its volumes and addresses. Stopping a stopped instance changes nothing. The operation is done once the instance is `STOPPED`, or failed once it is `FAILED`.

```sh
origin compute stop-instance [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The instance to stop. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |


|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |

Lists a project's key pairs, oldest first.

```sh

```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most key pairs to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### create-key-pair

Creates a key pair: imports `--public-key`, or, left empty, generates an `ssh-ed25519` key and returns its private half in `privateKey`, in this response only. A repeat of a generating request with the same `--request-id` can't return the private key again, and is refused with `CONFLICT`, its `ErrorInfo` metadata naming the key pair under `keyPair`: delete it and create another.

```sh
origin compute create-key-pair [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--public-key <PUBLIC_KEY>` | no | The OpenSSH public key line, such as `ssh-ed25519 AAAA... comment`. Left empty, the platform generates the key pair. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | no | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows, and the comment of a generated key. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id creates no second key pair. A repeat importing a key returns the first request's key pair; a repeat generating one is refused with `CONFLICT`, as the private key went to the first request only, and the error's `ErrorInfo` metadata names the key pair under `keyPair`. One is generated when not given. |

As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-tags` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-tags` | one of `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Remove all of its tags. |

| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-public-image

Returns a public image.

```sh
origin compute get-public-image [OPTIONS] --image <IMAGE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--image <IMAGE>` | yes | The image to return, `zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. Its id, completed with `--zone`, or its whole name, `zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. |

### list-public-images

Lists the public images in a zone, oldest first.

```sh
origin compute list-public-images [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone to list, such as `eu-central1-az1`. Without it, every zone that offers the service is listed, in catalog order; the profile's `default-zone` isn't used for lists. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most images to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |

### get-volume-attachment

Returns a volume attachment. A detached attachment isn't found.

```sh
origin compute get-volume-attachment [OPTIONS] --volume-attachment <VOLUME_ATTACHMENT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | no | The `{instance}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--volume-attachment` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--volume-attachment <VOLUME_ATTACHMENT>` | yes | The attachment to return. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone` and `--instance`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}/volumeAttachments/{volume_attachment}`. |

### list-volume-attachments

Lists an instance's volume attachments, the boot volume's first, then by device name. With `-` for the instance, lists every instance's in the zone, which with `--volume` finds the instance holding a volume. Detached attachments aren't listed.

```sh
origin compute list-volume-attachments [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone to list, such as `eu-central1-az1`. Without it, every zone that offers the service is listed, in catalog order; the profile's `default-zone` isn't used for lists. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The `{instance}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most attachments to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |
| `--volume <VOLUME>` | no | Only the attachments of this volume; every volume's when left empty. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/volumes/{volume}`. |

### create-volume-attachment

Attaches an `AVAILABLE` volume to a `RUNNING` or `STOPPED` instance in the same project and zone. On a stopped instance the disk appears at the next start, and the operation is done at once. On a running one it is added live, and the operation is done once the guest sees it, or failed if it couldn't be added, which leaves the volume available.

```sh
origin compute create-volume-attachment [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE> --volume <VOLUME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The `{instance}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--volume <VOLUME>` | yes | The volume, in the instance's project and zone. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/volumes/{volume}`. |
| `--device <DEVICE>` | no | The device name the guest sees the volume under, `vda` to `vdz`. The first free one when left empty. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of attaching again. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### delete-volume-attachment

Detaches a volume, which then is `AVAILABLE` again. The boot volume can't be detached. On a running instance the device is removed live; if the guest doesn't release it, the operation fails and the volume stays attached. The operation is done once the volume is detached.

```sh
origin compute delete-volume-attachment [OPTIONS] --volume-attachment <VOLUME_ATTACHMENT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | no | The `{instance}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--volume-attachment` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--volume-attachment <VOLUME_ATTACHMENT>` | yes | The attachment to delete, detaching its volume. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone` and `--instance`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}/volumeAttachments/{volume_attachment}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-operation

Returns an operation as it is now. The operation is one an `origin compute` command answered with, such as the one `--no-wait` prints.

```sh
origin compute get-operation [OPTIONS] --operation <OPERATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--operation <OPERATION>` | yes | The operation. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/operations/{operation}`. |

### wait-operation

Waits until an operation is done or `--timeout` has passed, whichever comes first, and returns it as it is then. It only reads, so a client may repeat it after a transport error. The operation is one an `origin compute` command answered with, such as the one `--no-wait` prints. Without `--timeout`, the command waits until the operation is done; Ctrl-C stops the waiting, not the operation. It prints the operation, and exits with status 1 when the operation failed, or isn't done when `--timeout` passes.

```sh
origin compute wait-operation [OPTIONS] --operation <OPERATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--operation <OPERATION>` | yes | The operation. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/operations/{operation}`. |
| `--timeout <DURATION>` | no | How long to wait for the operation, such as `30s` or `5m`. Without it, the command waits as long as the operation takes. When it passes first, the command prints the operation as it is and exits with status 1. |
